input: Scan and digitize all old family photo albums

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of albums and total photo count determines the scale of effort, time, and storage needed — a handful of albums is a weekend project; dozens could take months.
Whether the user will DIY with a home scanner, use a smartphone app, or hire a professional digitization service completely changes the cost, quality, and timeline of the plan.
If multiple family members are sharing the final files, decisions about access, sharing platforms, and permissions affect the output format and distribution plan.
The physical condition and age of the photos (e.g., faded, stuck to album pages, loose prints vs. mounted) affects handling requirements and whether restoration work is needed.
The desired resolution and quality (archival-grade TIFF vs. shareable JPEG) directly drives scanner settings, file sizes, storage needs, and whether professional equipment is required.
Where the digital files will ultimately live — a hard drive, cloud service, shared family platform — determines what tools, storage capacity, and organization system to set up.
Whether the user wants photos simply stored as-is or also organized, labeled, captioned, or edited (e.g., color correction, restoration) dramatically expands or narrows the scope of the task.

gold.taskTitle: Scan and digitize all old family photo albums
gold.taskDescription: Convert a collection of physical family photo albums into digital format, organized and preserved for long-term access.

questions.title: How many albums and roughly how many photos total?
questions.description: Establish the overall volume of physical material to be digitized, which sets the scale for time, effort, and storage planning.

questions.title: Will you scan them yourself or use a service?
questions.description: Determine whether the user plans to DIY with a home scanner or app, or outsource to a professional digitization service, which dictates cost, quality, and workflow.

questions.title: What condition are the photos and albums in?
questions.description: Understand whether photos are loose, mounted, faded, torn, or fragile, as this affects handling, scanning method, and whether restoration is needed.

questions.title: Who will have access to the final digital collection?
questions.description: Clarify whether the files are just for the user or shared with family members, which influences the sharing platform, folder structure, and file format choices.

questions.title: What scan quality or resolution do you need?
questions.description: Determine whether the goal is archival-grade high-resolution files or standard shareable images, which drives scanner settings and storage requirements.

questions.title: Where will the digitized photos be stored long-term?
questions.description: Identify the intended storage destination — external hard drive, cloud service, family sharing platform — to plan the right tools and organization system.

questions.title: Should photos just be saved, or also labeled and organized?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants photos stored as scanned or also sorted, captioned, dated, or color-corrected, which significantly changes the scope of work.
